..
KEY MESSAGE 1...A powerful coastal storm is expected to bring 
severe impacts to the region due to damaging high winds starting
late tonight, peaking during Thanksgiving Day, and departing 
into Friday.

Confidence is high that a powerful coastal storm will bring severe 
impacts to the area on Thanksgiving Day. The storm will continue
to strengthen and progress northward towards the area overnight
tonight.

Synoptics:

A strong upper-low will shift eastward out of the central US, with 
strong divergence aloft favoring surface cyclogenesis just off the 
southeast coast. From there, the low is expected to track northward 
while remaining inland towards the Mid Atlantic through Thursday. 
Guidance remains quite consistent on the development and rapid 
deepening of this low, and remains mostly in good agreement as far 
as timing and the storm track. The GFS, RGEM, and ECMWF all track 
the low northward from the coast of the Carolinas northward towards 
western PA.

A ~1044 mb high will be in place near the Gulf of Maine tonight, 
which will shift eastward toward Nova Scotia into Thursday. 
Meanwhile, the ~995 mb surface low will race northward into 
Thursday. This will create a very strong pressure gradient across 
our region, with surface pressure falls of near 35 mb in 24 hours 
(greater than 1 mb/hour) locally. A powerful low level jet is 
forecast to develop in response ahead of the low and sweep northward 
along the coast, with 925 mb winds in the 70-80 kts range. Notably, 
the 925 mb level is below the marine layer inversion, however the 
mixed boundary layer will be shallower than this (~1000 feet deep or 
so). Even then, GFS BUFKIT profiles indicate winds speeds within the 
mixed layer in the 50-60 kts range across the coastal plain of NJ 
and Delmarva, and in the 45-55 kts range as far inland as the Philly 
metro, southeastern PA, and portions of northern NJ. Due to the 
dynamics and thermodynamics of this storm, we anticipate these 
boundary layer winds to mix down to the surface in the form of 
widespread, frequent wind gusts of 50-70 mph, strongest near the 
coast and across Delmarva.

Impacts:

We now have high confidence in specific impacts across much of the 
area.

Winds: The most severe impact from this storm aside from coastal 
flooding (see separate coastal flooding key message below) will be 
from damaging high winds. Northeast to east winds will begin ramping 
up through tonight before peaking Thursday. Gusts of 50 to 70 mph 
are likely across our entire area, including inland. The strongest 
winds are expected to occur along the coast and inland across the 
coastal plain of Delmarva and southern NJ. Gusts could potentially 
exceed 70 mph during heavy rainbands along the Atlantic coasts of 
New Jersey and Delaware. Sustained winds along the immediate coast 
will be near 35-45 mph, potentially briefly stronger during heavy 
rainbands. A High Wind Warning is in effect for almost all of our 
area, where confidence is high in wind gusts reaching 60-70 mph. A 
Wind Advisory is in effect for Sussex and Morris Counties in NJ for 
wind gusts in the 45-55 mph range, although wind gusts may reach 60 
mph along ridge lines and mountain peaks in this area. The Warnings 
and Advisories are in effect starting late tonight through Thursday 
evening. Widespread tree damage and power outages are likely across 
much of our area during Thanksgiving Day, especially toward the 
coast and across Delmarva. The winds are expected to subside 
overnight Thursday night, however some guidance suggests southwest 
to west winds will increase with gusts near 35 to 45 mph possible 
again Friday afternoon and evening.

Rain: Given recent dryness and the progressive nature of this 
system, freshwater flooding does not appear to be as significant of 
a concern (compared to the high winds and tidal flooding). However 
it should be noted that forecast guidance continues to trend with 
higher with QPF...now suggesting near and S/E of the urban corridor 
a widespread 2 to 3.5 inches is likely with locally over 4 inches 
possible, especially over Delmarva and coastal NJ. The Weather 
Prediction Center has all of the area in at least a MARGINAL risk 
for excessive rainfall and has expanded the SLIGHT risk north and 
west through the I--95 corridor. The biggest threat will be urban 
flooding as well as flooding of low lying and poor drainage areas. 
Some of the more sensitive creeks and streams could also exceed 
flood stage. Finally, the heavy rain will exacerbate the coastal 
flooding issues. The heaviest rain will fall during the day 
Thursday into the first part of the evening before it starts to 
taper off. Some showers are likely to linger on Friday, 
especially northwest of I-95, but any rainfall on Friday will be
inconsequential.

Severe Weather: Areas across southern Delmarva just south of our 
county warning area are in a Marginal threat for severe 
thunderstorms SPC. The period of concern will be late afternoon
Thursd
